title: Logarithmically many half-balanced splits on every retained binary Hayes Haar layer
statement: Let ell >= 200, let n be 2 ell + 1 or 2 ell + 2, put c_0=ell-ceil(log2 ell)-2, and fix c_0 < j <= ell. Let M_0=F_j(global), and for 1 <= i <= c_0 let M_i be the level-j sibling-difference square mass over parents projecting to the identity in E_i. Then at least ceil(log2(16 ell^2)) indices i satisfy 2 M_i <= M_(i-1).

provenance.source: Axeyum gf2-lemire lane; nested identity-path sufficient bridge to polynomial delocalization

notes: The native identity_cylinder_path_split_implication operation proves this statement implies F:gf2-hayes-identity-cylinder-polynomial-share, hence the quarter-scale identity variance, REL, and the Lemire endpoint after the checked degree-400 handoff. At ell=200 it requires 20 half-balanced steps among 190 available coarse levels. Translation f(x)->f(x+1) proves one exact half-balanced split at level 2^v2(n) whenever that level lies on the path, leaving 19 at n=401 and n=402; power-of-two degrees show that this symmetry does not complete the universal statement. Other exact finite path reports are diagnostics only and are deliberately not attached as universal proof evidence. No Autogenesis operation is registered because no uniform checker establishes the remaining split inequalities.
